title: Client Statement and Portfolio Extraction
summary: Read CAS, mutual fund, broker, PMS and AIF statements into one consolidated, reconciled portfolio, with every holding linked to its source page and exceptions sent to operations.

seo.title: CAS and Portfolio Statement Extraction AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that reads CAS, mutual fund, broker, PMS and AIF statements, maps holdings to ISINs, reconciles totals and builds a consolidated client portfolio.

problem.intro: A new wealth client rarely arrives with one tidy statement. They bring a depository CAS, mutual fund statements from the registrars, a PMS quarterly report, an AIF capital account statement, bank deposit receipts and perhaps an overseas brokerage statement, and the RM's team rebuilds the portfolio by hand before any review can begin.

pain_points.title: Manual portfolio rebuilding
pain_points.detail: Operations staff copy holdings into spreadsheets, often for several family members and entities at once, and the work repeats at every review.

pain_points.title: Inconsistent names and identifiers
pain_points.detail: The same scheme or bond appears under different names across statements, and missing ISINs or plan variants cause wrong mappings.

pain_points.title: Double counting
pain_points.detail: Mutual fund units held in demat form can appear in both the depository CAS and a registrar statement, inflating the portfolio if nobody notices.

pain_points.title: Password-protected and scanned files
pain_points.detail: Statements arrive password-protected, scanned or as phone photos, which slows teams down and tempts staff to keep passwords insecurely.

solution.overview: We build a statement pipeline that accepts client statements by secure upload, email or, where your setup supports it, Account Aggregator data. It opens password-protected files in memory using the password the client provides, identifies the statement type and extracts holdings, transactions, valuations and statement dates. Each security is mapped to its ISIN or scheme code against your security master, and holdings that appear in more than one statement are de-duplicated. The pipeline reconciles extracted totals to each statement's own summary and sends unmapped securities or breaks to an operations analyst. The result is a consolidated portfolio in your wealth platform, ready for the adviser's review.
capabilities: Classifies statement types: depository CAS, registrar statements, broker holdings, PMS, AIF, deposits and overseas brokerage
Extracts holdings, transactions, units, NAV or price, valuation date and cost where shown
Maps securities to ISINs and scheme codes, including plan and option variants
De-duplicates holdings that appear in more than one statement
Reconciles extracted totals to each statement's own summary and flags breaks
Exports a consolidated portfolio by client, family member and asset class to your wealth platform

workflow.title: Collect statements with consent
workflow.detail: Clients share statements through a secure upload, email or Account Aggregator consent, and the consent is recorded.

workflow.title: Open and classify
workflow.detail: Password-protected files are opened in memory, and each statement is classified by type and source.

workflow.title: Extract holdings and transactions
workflow.detail: Holdings, transactions and valuations are extracted with page references.

workflow.title: Map and de-duplicate
workflow.detail: Securities are mapped to ISINs or scheme codes, and duplicate holdings across statements are merged.

workflow.title: Reconcile and review
workflow.detail: Totals are reconciled to statement summaries; breaks and unmapped items go to an operations analyst.

workflow.title: Publish the portfolio
workflow.detail: The consolidated portfolio is pushed to the wealth platform for the adviser's review.

inputs: NSDL or CDSL consolidated account statements
Registrar mutual fund statements from CAMS or KFintech
Broker holding statements and contract notes
Bank deposit and bond holding statements
Security master with ISINs and scheme codes
outputs: Consolidated holdings by client, family member and asset class
Transaction history with cost where the statement provides it
Mapping exceptions for unknown or ambiguous securities
Export to the wealth platform or Excel
human_in_the_loop: Operations analysts resolve every unmapped security and reconciliation break before a portfolio is published. Advisers review the consolidated portfolio before any client discussion, and the system never suggests what to buy, sell or switch.
integrations: Wealth management or portfolio management platform
Account Aggregator ecosystem, where you are onboarded as a financial information user
Secure client upload portal and email
guardrails: Statement passwords used in memory only and never stored
PAN and account numbers masked in logs
Reconciliation to statement totals required before publishing
Every holding linked to its source page
No recommendations or advice generated from the data
compliance_notes: Client consent is recorded before statements are processed, supporting DPDP Act 2023 requirements on consent and purpose.
Outputs are analytical inputs for SEBI-registered advisers or distributors; the system does not generate investment advice.

pilot.scope: A set of de-identified client statement bundles covering depository CAS, registrar statements and PMS reports, processed in parallel with your operations team.

Timed with and without the pipeline on a sample of bundles.

faqs.q: Can it read password-protected CAS files?
faqs.a: Yes, using the password the client provides for that upload. The password is used in memory to open the file and is never stored.

faqs.q: Does it handle overseas brokerage and custody statements?
faqs.a: Yes, with a schema per statement format. New formats can be added without templates, and the first statements from any new source are reviewed by an analyst.

faqs.q: Will it suggest rebalancing or switches?
faqs.a: No. It produces a clean, reconciled portfolio. Analysis and recommendations remain with your registered advisers.
It extracts transactions and cost where statements provide them, which your tax or portfolio tools can use. Where cost data is missing, it flags the gap rather than estimating.
